The barycentric-gradient projection B=G^{-1}-(G^{-1}1)(G^{-1}1)^T/S has B_aa=(4w_a^2/n)(1-6/[n(n^2-1)]), whence the unique equal-facet incenter weights w_a/W and r^2=9/[(n^2-1)(n(n^2-1)-6)]. Solving equal-distance linear equations gives strictly positive circumcenter coefficients: (n-1)/(2n) on terminal cuts plus 1/n of the incenter. The weighted sum of squared distances proves minimum-enclosing uniqueness and its exact R^2. det K=n^(n-2), det G=n^(n-2)/(2^(n-1) ((n-1)!)^4); det of differences=det G*S proves face volume squared. Independently reconstructed rational matrix cases n=3..5 agree; source checker uses n=3..10. Strictly these checks corroborate, while second difference/Gram formulas prove n>=3.
